Q: Automatically growing lists in Python A:

Sure it's possible, you just have to use a subclass of list to do it.

class GrowingList(list):
    def __setitem__(self, index, value):
        if index >= len(self):
            self.extend([None]*(index + 1 - len(self)))
        list.__setitem__(self, index, value)

Usage:

>>> grow = GrowingList()
>>> grow[10] = 4
>>> len(grow)
11
>>> grow
[None, None, None, None, None, None, None, None, None, None, 4]

Just note that this is only really useful for dense arrays. If you need a structure for sparse arrays, then you are better off with a dictionary based solution.

Q: How do I make a manually-added value in a choice column persist? A:

I created a new list on my Office365 SharePoint site. When in classic mode, manually entered values are not available, while editing/creating new list items regardless of the choices are displayed in a dropdown, radio buttons or as multi select checkboxes.

When switching from the classic to the modern SharePoint experience, manually entered values are available while editing/adding list items.

Q: Kotlin daemon compilation failed: Could not connect to Kotlin daemon process in Android Studio A:

Your step 4 did nothing. org.gradle.kotlin.daemon.enabled is not a real property, so it was silently ignored. That is why the error never changed.

Workaround (correct property): in gradle.properties

kotlin.compiler.execution.strategy=in-process

Actual fix: the daemon is a separate JVM that fails to start. Find out why:

%USERPROFILE%\.kotlin\daemon\

Read the newest .log there. It names the real cause.

Usual culprits:

  1. Oversized org.gradle.jvmargs. If you have -Xmx8G on a 16 GB machine, there is nothing left for the Kotlin daemon to allocate. Drop it to -Xmx4g.

  2. Give the daemon its own limit:

    kotlin.daemon.jvmargs=-Xmx2g

  3. Windows Defender / antivirus blocking the local socket the daemon connects over. Exclude your project folder and %USERPROFILE%\.gradle.

Clean slate before retrying:

gradlew --stop

Then delete %USERPROFILE%\.kotlin\daemon and %USERPROFILE%\.gradle\daemon.

Note that in-process makes builds slower and pushes Kotlin compilation into the Gradle daemon's heap, so treat it as a diagnostic rather than a permanent setting.
